text:
22:28 - fact check: Mr Morale and the Big Steppers dropped in 2022 went #1, won rap album of the year at the Grammys, and had a record breaking solo rap tour at the time. Mr. Morale has 3.5 billion total streams on Spotify and gets 1.5 million daily streams in 2025. MMBS already has more total streams and daily streams on Spotify than every single J. Cole album except 2014 Forest Hills Drive. MMBS has a higher metacritic rating (85 critics, 88 users) than every J.Cole album including Forest Hills Drive.

There is no way you can say it was a bad album by any stretch or that it flopped or isn’t played. Cause it’s played today and in total more than every Cole album outside of FHD. But no one claims Born Sinner, For Your Eyes Only, KOD, and The Off Seasons are all flops… but if you compared them to Mr. Morale they have much less replay value (showed by total streams and daily streams) and much worse average critics and user ratings. 

You could only argue it’s not Dot’s best album —and a lot of ppl have it in their top 3 of his discography— but the success is undeniable and it’s actually an underrated album because the BS narrative that it flopped.

author: @renecardoza45
text: Kendrick coming for Drake is nothing new because they've been firing shots at each since the early 2010's (their relationship changed in 2013 when Drake publicly made it known that he was salty about the "Control" verse).  There may or may not be any real beef between the two to this day but I miss seeing rappers battle to prove they're #1.  I was shocked to see Kendrick taking some jabs at Cole.  I've been sitting with this verse for days and I still can't believe this shit lol.  I know that the two have love for each other so it's gonna be interesting to see how Cole responds on a track if he even responds at all.  It'd be fire to see Cole step in the ring and have some fun cause we all know he's got the bars to compete with anybody.  We don't see rappers going toe to toe for the top spot anymore and I think that that's a big part of the game thats lacking.  There's no competitiveness and no excitement in the game anymore.  Gotta appreciate Kendrick for always being the one to pop shit off and create some controversy.  Competition is the spark that's missing in the rap game and it's gonna be interesting to see what happens next.
